clue.text: Willing to defer loan by letter (10)

blocks.note: a sub is an advance or loan, as in 'sub me a tenner'
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Someone writes to ask whether a loan repayment can be put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defer' looks like the verb for postponing a loan, but it belongs to the definition: willing to defer means ready to give way. 'By' just sets SUB beside MISSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: the submissive give way to others' wishes, which is being willing to defer.

clue.text: Topless muscleman represented America (5,3)

indicators.note: a topless word loses its first letter
the letters are presented again in a new arrangement

blocks.note: MUSCLEMAN without its top letter M

explanation.surface: A bare-chested bodybuilder competed for the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a strongman at an international contest; Uncle Sam is the cartoon figure who personifies the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the national personification of the United States.

clue.text: Forced to remove English cross (3)

indicators.note: tells you to take a letter out

blocks.note: made = forced, as in 'made me do it'
E = English, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone was compelled to take down an English crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' sits at the end looking like a noun, a crucifix or a mark; it is the adjective meaning angry, which in American use is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad can mean angry, the same as cross.

clue.text: Doctor’s cut about to produce rapid swelling (5)

indicators.note: says a piece has been taken away

blocks.note: a surgeon is a doctor
on = about, concerning, the part that is cut

explanation.surface: A doctor's incision causes a quick swelling of the flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the ’s as 'has': the doctor has 'about' cut from him, so SURGEON loses ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden, rapid rise or swell.

clue.text: Passes on major road having elevated sections (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a piece up writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway; with the digit 1 as I, elevated it reads upward
parts = sections

explanation.surface: A stretch of motorway runs over flyovers in places.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords let the digit 1 stand for the letter I, so the M1 written upward gives IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart something is to pass it on, like knowledge.

clue.text: Political forecasts from Split, by outspoken Europeans (4,5)

indicators.note: spoken out loud: the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: split = leave, make an exit
Poles are Europeans

explanation.surface: Election predictions come from a Croatian city, with help from vocal Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is capitalised to look like the Croatian port; it is the slang verb for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Exit polls, taken as voters leave, forecast election results.

clue.text: Fell race (4)

blocks.note: fell is an old word for an animal's hide, not the hill in Cumbria
race as a verb: to rush along at full speed

explanation.surface: A race run over the fells, the hills of northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell running is hill racing in the English Lake District, so the two words look like one sport; a pelt is a skin, and to pelt is to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell and pelt both mean an animal hide; pelt also means to rush.

clue.text: A Parisian who places tips (11)

blocks.note: per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
qui is French for who
sites = places

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who hands out gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Parisian' looks like one unit, a Frenchman; the A is its own piece, PER, and 'Parisian' belongs to 'who'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perquisites are extra payments or perks, and tips count among them.

clue.text: Songs first in the race to be heard (6)

indicators.note: the word is to be listened to, not read

blocks.note: the leader is first in a race

explanation.surface: Singing at the front of the field so everyone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert; the German word is said 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder is the German plural for songs, used for classical German art songs.

clue.text: Sweet and sour dip (4,4)

blocks.note: acid = sour
a dip is a drop

explanation.surface: Sweet and sour sauce served as a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the Chinese-restaurant sauce; an acid drop is a sharp-tasting boiled sweet sold in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid drop is a tart boiled sweet, a British candy.

clue.text: King backed by two-thirds of his country (6)

indicators.note: a backed word is written backwards
keep two of the three letters

blocks.note: two of the three letters of HIS
King Lear, Shakespeare's king; backed, it reads RAEL

explanation.surface: A monarch supported by most of his subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' only sets the two pieces side by side; IS comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Israel is a Middle Eastern state, and the clue just calls it a country.

clue.text: Bully people to serve without reply (6)

blocks.note: men = people
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return

explanation.surface: Intimidating people into serving you without talking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' looks like doing someone's bidding; it is the tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to menace is to threaten, which is what a bully does to people.

clue.text: A writer’s bar bursting with muscatel (6,5)

indicators.note: the letters of BAR burst open and mix with the rest

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An author's local pub is packed with sweet wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ’s as 'is': a writer is the anagram. Muscatel is a sweet dessert wine, and a writer in a bar is a familiar picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French writer, author of The Outsider.

clue.text: Transports unopened bags by river (8)

indicators.note: the word has lost its opening letter
sets one piece beside the other

blocks.note: R = river, as on maps
CAPTURES (bags) without its first letter

explanation.surface: Lorries carry sealed sacks along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transports' looks like vehicles or carrying; it means ecstasies, being carried away with joy. Bags means nets or catches, as a hunter bags game.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in its old sense is being carried away by emotion, and raptures are exactly such fits of ecstasy.

clue.text: Where flogging occurs behind saloons? (3,4,5)

blocks.note: read as a place of whipping, and meant as British slang for selling: flogging is flogging goods
read as round the back of Wild West bars, and meant as at the rear of saloon cars, from the boot

explanation.surface: Where whippings take place at the back of Wild West bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Flogging is British slang for selling, and saloons are sedan cars; a car boot sale is a British flea market where people sell things from the boots (trunks) of their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: At car boot sales goods are sold from the back of parked cars.

clue.text: Marking helping to support pupil once (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece goes underneath

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
a serving is a helping of food

explanation.surface: A teacher's grading helps prop up a struggling former student.
explanation.walkthrough: Marking is the verb for observing an occasion, as in marking an anniversary, not grading homework as the pupil suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark a festival or anniversary is to keep it, and observing carries the same sense of honouring the day.

clue.text: One might get a stiff back cured by him (8)

definitions.text: One might get a stiff back cured by him

blocks.clueFragment: One might get a stiff back
blocks.note: read as a patient with back pain, and meant as a corpse, a stiff, being handed back
read as healed by a physio, and meant as preserved, the way meat is cured

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist fixes patients with a stiff back.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, and cured means preserved rather than healed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff is slang for a corpse and curing means preserving, so the man who preserves bodies is the one meant.

clue.text: Wait for a PC to come back (8,4)

definitions.text: Wait for a PC to come back

blocks.note: read as sitting in front of a slow personal computer, and meant as waiting for a police constable
read as the machine replying, and meant as the officer turning up after your call

explanation.surface: Waiting for a slow computer to respond.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer; it is also a police constable, and response time is how long police take to arrive after a call.
explanation.definitionFit: PC as police constable: the wait for police to arrive after an emergency call is measured as their response time.

clue.text: Figure love can’t go wrong (7)

indicators.note: the letters go awry into a new order

blocks.note: love = O, zero in tennis
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A romantic insists love is foolproof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' does double duty in the surface, but the anagram needs its letters as fodder: CANT GO plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an eight-sided shape is one kind of geometric figure.

clue.text: Cowboy being awkward, mostly over nothing (6)

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of it, so the word is cut short by its final letter
in a down clue, sits on top of the next piece

blocks.note: GAUCHE (awkward) without its last letter
O = nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A clumsy cowboy is making a fuss about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaucho is a South American cowboy of the pampas.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: the gaucho is the horseman of the South American pampas, their equivalent of a cowboy.

clue.text: Vehicles going head-to-head to secure a game (8)

indicators.note: the two vehicles meet front to front, so the first one faces backwards
to secure something is to hold it fast, so CART grips the A inside it

blocks.note: one vehicle, a cab, turned round to BAC
the other vehicle, a cart, which holds A
the A secured inside CART

explanation.surface: Two cars meet in a head-on crash while collecting a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Head-to-head means nose to nose: CAB reads backwards so that its front meets the front of CART.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: baccarat is one card game among many, played in casinos.

clue.text: Italian uniform that is trimmed with leather (6)

indicators.note: an edging of leather goes round the outside

blocks.note: to tan is to beat, leather someone; tan is also leather's colour; it wraps the rest
U = uniform in the NATO alphabet
sc. = scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'

explanation.surface: An Italian uniform with leather trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a smart Italian outfit; Tuscan is someone from Tuscany in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: people from Tuscany, the region round Florence, are one kind of Italian.

clue.text: Egg on top of toast abandoned unfinished (5)

indicators.note: the first letter, the top in a down clue
the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: the top letter of TOAST
EMPTY (abandoned) without its last letter

explanation.surface: An egg on toast left half-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' looks like the food on the toast; as a verb 'egg on' means urge, and the definition is the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: egging someone on is urging them, and to tempt is to lure them into doing it.

clue.text: Seafood starter to improve on urchin (6)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows
placed after, as an across clue builds left to right

blocks.note: an urchin is a mischievous child, a rascal; not the sea creature
first letter of IMPROVE

explanation.surface: A seafood starter that makes sea urchin taste better.
explanation.walkthrough: Urchin sits among seafood to look like a sea urchin; it is a street child, a scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Daring to include this setter really is playful (8)

blocks.note: game = willing, plucky
so = really, as in 'so good'
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A setter slips in a bold remark about how much fun they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamesome is an old word for frisky or sportive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamesome means playful and full of fun.

clue.text: Audible like this note (3)

indicators.note: audible means able to be heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: so = like this, in this way

explanation.surface: Hear it: this is the note.
explanation.walkthrough: Soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale, do re mi fa soh.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: soh, the fifth step of the tonic sol-fa scale, is one musical note.

clue.text: Tutors in demand on Sundays (4)

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow

blocks.note: demanD ON Sundays

explanation.surface: Private tutors are much sought after on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In demand' reads as one phrase, popular; the 'in' is the signal and the answer runs across 'demand on Sundays'. Dons are Oxford and Cambridge teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dons are university tutors, especially at Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: I got out of tracing that complex timeline plan (5,5)

indicators.note: the I got out of the phrase, escaping it, so that letter is removed
the remaining letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: TRACING THAT with the I taken out

explanation.surface: Someone escapes having to trace an intricate project schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is the clue's first word, the letter itself. A Gantt chart is a bar chart of tasks against time, used in project management.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gantt chart plans a project's tasks along a timeline.
